correctness.rationale: Conditioning on the frozen arrows leaves two independent uniform targets. An arrow into the sink basin closes exactly one cycle and an arrow outside closes none. A single inside target gives either sign with equal weight k(n−k)/n²; it is uniform in the rooted tree, yielding the path mark. Cayley counting with the specified basin vertex set gives b(n,k), with K=n having mass 1/n and only a zero jump. Rooted forest extension of a prescribed depth-h path gives a(k,h)=(h+1)(k−1)_h/k^(h+1). This equals t_h−t_(h+1) for t_h=(k−1)_h/k^h, so its tail at h≈r√k tends to exp(−r²/2). The one-sign basin weight is (n−k)/n² times the binomial mass at k for success probability k/n. Stirling gives its interior density at scale n^(−3/2), with uniform envelope proportional to u^(−1/2)(1−u)^(1/2), whose endpoint contributions vanish as the truncation is removed. Its integral with the normalizing factor 1/√(2π) is √(π/8), giving the beta mark and the total rate. The conditional basin size tends to infinity in probability; the depth kernel then yields independent Rayleigh after division by √K, and multiplication by √(K/n) gives the asserted joint mark. Independently enumerated n=3 masses per sign are 8/81, 2/81, 2/81 at (1,1), (2,1), (2,2) (branches/e546cb88-f6d2-4a5d-96ef-cc3b4006ef5a/independent_n3.py and independent_n3.txt). Frozen verify.py was inspected, not executed.
